newsitem.title: UK: UK to widen rules for conditional access services.
newsitem.headline: UK to widen rules for conditional access services.

text.p: Britain unveiled plans on Thursday to extend regulation of conditional access services to non-broadcast services in the digital age.

"Conditional access services can form an important bottleneck to competition in supply of all kinds of entertainment, information and interactive services (such as home shopping and home banking)," said Don Cruickshank, head of telecoms watchdog Oftel.

"It makes sense to extend the existing rules in order to promote fair and effective competition and enhance consumer choice across the full range of retail services delivered by digital communications networks," he added.
Oftel said it was seeking comments by August 14 on how to extend protection.
Conditional access is the system by which only those who are authorised to receive or use a particular service can do so.

British Telecommunciations Plc and BSkyB Plc are the largest partners in the BIB consortium which plans to launch home shopping and home banking services when digital satellite broadcasting begins in the UK next year.
